spatialBenefitAssessment: The current mechanism is a temporal approval-state example better served by the recommended Astra video. That transcript already shows A approved, B mismatched, B freshly reviewed and B executed. The candidate adds a tiny hidden keyed profile and selectable timing, but no independently variable relationship beyond that sequence. Hiding artifact equality under a crate does not establish spatial value. Omit this candidate unless a fundamentally different scope-binding investigation proves useful.

findings.issue: The key/lock metaphor repeats the video and hides an arbitrary encoding under the crates.
findings.requestedChange: For a substantially different attempt, investigate approval scope: keep the artifact fixed while redirecting it between staging and production, and separately change the artifact while holding the target fixed. Represent independent artifact and target bindings as two inspectable interlocks; use one control to cycle proposals and one to approve the exact proposal. Compare this against a simple 2D matrix before committing to 3D.
findings.evidence: Recommended Astra transcript covers the entire A/B sequence. interaction.js uses waiting===approved; target never varies. intent acknowledges the small guided counterfactual space.

findings.issue: Enabled buttons silently discard input while animations run.
findings.requestedChange: Disable both primary controls whenever moves.length or recut is nonzero, then refresh enabled state when the final tween/recut completes; alternatively queue one explicit pending action and display that state. Keep Reset available.
findings.evidence: onRun and onRevise return early during moves/recut, but refresh disabled conditions omit animation state. User explicitly reported ignored Run clicks after Revise/Review. captures/revision-blocked.png shows a waiting B and swap caption, NOT a blocked result; reviewer did not reproduce the click.

findings.issue: The default view does not expose the alleged physical fit; the authored blocked stop actually leaves a gap before contact.
findings.requestedChange: If retained, make a close end-on comparison the starting view and use a shallow cutaway that simultaneously exposes the relevant teeth and plate. Adjust the stop to show actual interference or explicitly call it a pre-execution mismatch check rather than a collision. Provide equivalent keyboard access through existing controls.
findings.evidence: Initial and revision-blocked images show dark keels beneath opaque bodies without a readable fit. Gate pick alone invokes [6.2,0.8,0]. In build_scene.py, blocked crate center is 0.905; tooth leading edge is center+0.63=1.535, before plate near face 1.565. Caption says keel hits plate, but source leaves 0.03 units clearance.

findings.issue: A clearance profile encodes one-sided fit, not exact identity; approval identity is asserted by strings independently of the geometry.
findings.requestedChange: Use a two-sided keyed comparison or a visibly separate exact-identity comparator if this mechanism survives. Keep the metaphor explicitly scoped and never suggest that a looser/smaller physical profile is sufficient authorization. Verify the recut geometry for both identities.
findings.evidence: build_scene.py builds varying tooth depths and clearance below each tooth; smaller teeth could clear an unmatched profile. onRun checks string identity, not geometric fit. This is acceptable scripted behavior only if the visible metaphor faithfully communicates exact matching.

requiredVerification: No live browser tests were run by this reviewer. The ignored-click behavior is attributed to the user and corroborated by source; revision-blocked.png is only a waiting-state capture.
If retained, verify clicks during and after both revision and review animations; capture actual stale-B denial after motion settles, and fresh-B execution separately.
Capture exact profile alignment from the gate view at desktop and 420px; verify nearest-visible picking, gate/frame occlusion, keyboard access and reduced motion.
Verify Reset during every transition and final state; prove an independent scope-binding counterfactual before reconsidering omission.
